topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by introducing the course themes and outlining the learning objectives regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Concepts and epidemiology of cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the interplay between intrinsic genetic mutations, bad luck, and environmental exposures in driving cancer development and population-level incidence.

topics.label: Pathogens and infectious agents in carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious pathogens contribute to cancer development, focusing on the mechanism and epidemiology of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how various chemical and physical agents undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion and non-mutagenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics distinguish tumor promoters from initiators, examining how non-mutagenic stimuli like chronic inflammation drive cell proliferation.

topics.label: Host tissue susceptibility and summary of carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how host developmental timing influences cancer susceptibility and summarize the major mechanisms of carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the molecular, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro approaches used to determine whether specific agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion and risk-benefit perspective
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation by considering everyday risk-benefit decisions regarding carcinogen exposure and summarizing the lecture.
